 Home » Tabloid »  Hyderabad Chronicle A Musical Heirloom for Sam’s Baby
 Hyderabad Chronicle Apsara Reddy 19 Nov 2026 7:40 PM IST 19 Nov 2026 7:40 PM IST A family reunion, sacred chants and a song composed especially for the baby. Samantha’s Seemantam, hosted by husband Raj Nidimoru’s family, was less about ceremony and more about the beautiful art of bringing generations together
 x Dressed in red, Samantha received the elders’ blessings as the family gathered around her. (DC) As Preferred
Source Dressed in red, Samantha received the elders’ blessings as the family gathered around her. For Sheetal, the occasion was long-awaited. “When can we do this, Babu?” she recalled asking her brother. The gathering reunited the women Sheetal calls her “pinnammas” and “peddamma”, the aunts who helped raise the siblings.
 They chanted, sang and laughed “like girlfriends”, recreating the warmth of family gatherings from Raj and Sheetal’s childhood.
 Named Matru Shishu Mangala Ashirvadam, the ceremony included the recitation of Sri Suktam, a Gayatri Devi homam and 21 repetitions of the Gayatri Mantra. The rituals brought back memories of the family altar, where Raj and Sheetal grew up chanting with their grandparents and aunts.
 Their parents continued the tradition of bringing everyone together in prayer. “It reset the home, and us,” Sheetal wrote.
 The most personal offering was a song composed especially for Samantha and the baby by Padma Shri awardee Shobha Raju, one of the siblings’ aunts. Sheetal sang, her peddamma, Padma Shri awardee Vidushi Sumitra Guha, brought in the ragas, and Neeru aunty joined her. Raj and Sheetal’s mother and Usha aunty completed the chorus.
 Sheetal called it their “own little family production”. A celebration of music, prayer and generations of affection, the ceremony welcomed a new member into a family already singing for the little one.
 As Sheetal wrote, “Little one, look at all the love you’ve already brought together.”
 Highlight: Named Matru Shishu Mangala Ashirvadam featured sacred chants and a Gayatri Devi homam, evoking Raj and Sheetal’s childhood memories of family prayers. grandparents and aunts.
